subject: Staged capacity waiver and traffic safeguard for Helix preview
messages:
From: Bethany Lee <bethany@helixai.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 10:34:00 -0700
Subject: Request for temporary SLO buffer for preview launch

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the run-through on Friday. We're excited to move Helix's semantic-search preview into a limited prod cohort next month. Before we flip traffic, the ops team asked whether Redwood can consider a temporary SLO buffer for this preview window.

What we're asking: a 30-day pilot where availability SLO is relaxed to 98% (from our usual 99.9%) during business hours for the preview cohort and a latency guardrail allowance up to 350ms p95 (baseline target today is 200ms p95). The traffic will be throttled and routed by header so only ~5% of our overall traffic hits the preview model.

Why: the preview uses an experimental model variant with an updated encoder. We expect the model to be stable but want to avoid failed requests disrupting our users while we iterate. We'll provide a traffic schedule and fallbacks.

Attached: helix-preview-traffic.csv (sample distribution) and a draft MOU. Can Redwood provide a temporary carveout and a short-term operational playbook (rollback thresholds, on-call contacts, and routing rules)?

Appreciate any guidance on what exceptions look like (approval path, legal/ops signoff, monitoring hooks). Happy to jump on a call.

Best,
Bethany
Bethany Lee
Head of Product Operations, Helix AI
bethany@helixai.com
+1 (415) 555-0219

Bethany — thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the traffic sample.

Quick bullets on Redwood's side:
- We do support temporary SLO carveouts for gated previews but they require a short ops/leadership review + a documented rollback plan.
- Typical approvals: AM/AE + Product lead + Security/Legal if data residency or PII is involved. For performance relaxations we also loop in the runtime team for guardrails.
- We'll need a simple playbook (thresholds, who flips the switch, and an automatic fallback route).

Ben and Marcus — can you two help scope the technical mitigation and an estimated uplift on reserved capacity for the 5% traffic window? Marcus, please flag any model-specific runtime risks (kv-cache, warm-start CPU/GPU pressure).

Bethany — I'll draft a proposal for a staged capacity waiver and an operational runbook and route it to our internal approvers. Can you confirm the preview cohort start date (target window) and whether you require business-hours-only enforcement?

Thanks,

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Bethany Lee <bethany@helixai.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: staged capacity waiver + operational playbook for Helix preview (for approval)

Lauren / Soojin — looping you both in for approvals on a temporary SLO relaxation request from Helix AI (external). Key points below; draft proposal attached.

Summary: Helix requests a 30-day SLO buffer for a preview cohort (5% traffic) beginning 2027-05-10. Requested temporary targets: availability 98% (business hours) and latency p95 up to 350ms. Planned mitigations: header-based routing to a preview model variant, automatic fallback to stable model on 5xx/timeout, dedicated reserved capacity for the cohort (estimate below), and close monitoring with daily health emails + escalation to on-call.

Operational details (high-level):
- Reserved pool: 2 x A100-equivalent slots reserved during business hours for first 7 days, autoscale policy to add 1 slot if p95 > 350ms for two consecutive 15-min windows.
- Rollback thresholds: immediate rollback if error rate > 2% for 30m or if availability drops below 95% for any continuous 1h window.
- Monitoring hooks: webhook from Helix, Redwood can push token-level latency breakdown to shared dashboard.
- Approval path: Sales (Ben), Product Ops (Marcus), Legal/Security (Soojin), and VP rev (Lauren) signoff required before we open routing.

Risk assessment: medium — the experimental encoder can produce higher latency under specific token-length distributions. Mitigations above reduce blast radius; we will also disable autoretry and enforce short client-side timeouts for preview cohort.

Attached: slo-exception-proposal.pdf (operational playbook + risk register).

Bethany — if this looks good from Helix's side, Ben will route the draft exception term to Legal and Ops will schedule the reserved pool provisioning. Please confirm you will sign the MOU and accept the rollback conditions.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
